prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a residential meter/yard/backflow device or a commercial/industrial/fire‑line device? I can give specific local company names if you tell me which — otherwise here are the quickest, reliable ways to get testing and repair near Liberty, MO plus what to ask and what to expect.

Who to contact
- City of Liberty Utilities / Water Department — they often maintain a list of approved/certified backflow testers and can tell you whether test reports must be filed to the city. (Search “City of Liberty MO utilities” or call city hall.)
- Local plumbing companies that advertise backflow/backflow prevention testing.
- Irrigation/sprinkler companies — many are certified to test residential backflow assemblies.
- Fire sprinkler / fire protection contractors — they commonly service larger commercial backflow assemblies and fire-line backflow devices.
- Independent certified backflow testers (search “backflow tester Kansas City metro” or “backflow testing Liberty MO”).

What to ask a tester/company
- Are you a certified backflow assembly tester? What is your certification number? (Make them show proof.)
- Are you licensed and insured?
- Will you file/submit the test report to the City of Liberty (if required)? Or will you provide a copy I can give them?
- Do you service/repair the make and model of my device? (Have device make/model or photos ready.)
- Estimated fee for the annual test and a rough repair estimate if a leak or failed test is found.
- How soon can you come?

Typical costs (approximate)
- Annual residential backflow test: roughly $50–$125.
- Repairs or replacement parts: can range from $50 for simple parts to several hundred dollars for major repairs or a new device.
Prices vary by device type and the local market.

If you want, tell me: residential vs commercial and your ZIP code (or allow me to look up businesses). I can then provide a short list of likely local companies and phone numbers to call.
